![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14134102/assets/c3fe1a2a1181dadaa3f67a15e8128e4e6519cfcee3efbfb69ac597e454619247.png)

Which of the diagrams above shows three collinear points?
question.worked_solution:
Three (or more) points are collinear if a straight line passes through all points.

With that in mind, let's examine our diagrams in turn. 

- Diagram I shows three collinear points. There is a straight line that passes through all three of these points.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14134102/assets/d0889441a43b73e2b1abd1c504974e755325977cc2d3c4cfd86777c6ded4d106.png)

- Diagram II shows three points that are *not* collinear. We can't draw a straight line that passes through all three points.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14134102/assets/ead554eea443d790cfc642b2fc4c2c916829df373b701668c1f20b4b4299c369.png)

- Diagram III shows three points that are *not* collinear. We can't draw a straight line that passes through all three points.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14134102/assets/9d8d988f789cf9bfd8b026d6cd48fcabf43abe70c294a4fe1617e5a959f51b86.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
